method: sha256 over three 16 MiB windows per file (head, midpoint, tail) of each */inflated/0.raw. A prefilter, NOT an equality proof.
why_this_matters: Hardlink-dedup frees space WITHOUT deleting anything, which the certify-or-block rule prefers over any deletion. Confirming the two groups costs a full sha256 of five files (18.3 GB of reads); hardlinking then releases three files' worth of blocks.
why_sr5_did_not_act: The 61 GiB target was already being met by a class whose restore is a numpy slice of a sibling in the same directory, and this arm ran the prefilter late -- after deletions had begun. Acting on it would have meant building and reviewing a certified hardlink producer at the end of the run for space the arm did not need. It is handed forward as a measured, high-value, lossless door.
caution_from_sr4: Hardlinked files share future writes; any regeneration must target a fresh output path. sr4 performed its own hardlinks only after FULL source and destination hashes plus a custody audit.
